title: Dark mode for DuckDuckGo
question: How do I make DuckDuckGo dark without changing settings each time?
answer: DuckDuckGo has a Dark theme under Settings, and its default theme follows your system's dark mode, but the choice is stored in a cookie, so clearing cookies or opening a private window brings back the default theme, which is light unless your system is in dark mode. The usermods script on this page sets DuckDuckGo's own dark theme cookie before the page starts, so search results load dark on every visit. Without an extension, adding &kae=d to a search URL or bookmark gives the dark theme for that page.
prompt: Always show DuckDuckGo in its dark theme, even after I clear cookies.
details: DuckDuckGo stores the theme in a cookie named `ae`; `d` is Dark. The script writes that cookie at document start when it is missing or holds another theme, and DuckDuckGo's page code reads it and applies its own dark theme. Nothing else is restyled, so the page looks exactly like DuckDuckGo's Dark theme. It replaces any other theme picked in Settings. The check loads a results page with no cookies and confirms the background is dark and the results are there.

alternatives.title: Settings theme
alternatives.body: Open DuckDuckGo's settings from the menu at the top right of a results page and pick the Dark theme. It is saved in a cookie for this browser.

alternatives.title: URL parameter
alternatives.body: Add `&kae=d` to a search URL, or use `https://duckduckgo.com/?kae=d&q=%s` as the browser's search engine URL.

check.baseline: (() => { const [r, g, b] = getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor.match(/\d+/g).map(Number); return r + g + b > 600; })()
check.expect: (() => { const [r, g, b] = getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor.match(/\d+/g).map(Number); return r + g + b < 150 && document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark-bg'); })()
check.intact: (() => { const res = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="result"]')].filter((r) => r.checkVisibility()); const a = res[0] && res[0].querySelector('a[data-testid="result-title-a"]'); const c = a ? getComputedStyle(a).color.match(/\d+/g).map(Number) : [0, 0, 0]; return res.length >= 5 && c[0] + c[1] + c[2] > 300; })()
